title: Newborn Problems: Breathing, Warmth, Sugar and Transport

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already keep newborns warm, check blood glucose and support breathing. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Recognize newborn breathing problems that change your plan
  2. Prevent and treat cold and low sugar, using BC's numbers
  3. Spot seizures, dangerous vomiting and birth injuries, and transport wisely

Textbook: Chapter 43, PDF pages 3671–3707
slides.say: Welcome back. Last lesson we resuscitated a newborn. Today we look at the newborn who is breathing but in trouble. As EMRs, you already keep babies warm, check blood glucose and support breathing. As a PCP, you need to recognize which problems change your plan, use BC's glucose rules correctly, and choose the right destination. We'll cover three things: breathing problems and preterm babies; keeping newborns warm and treating low blood sugar; and seizures, dangerous vomiting, birth injuries and transport.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎回来。上节课我们复苏了一个新生儿；今天看的是有呼吸、但有麻烦的新生儿。作为 EMR，你们已经会给孩子保暖、测血糖、支持呼吸。作为 PCP，你要认出哪些问题会改变你的处理方案，正确运用 BC 的血糖规则，并选对目的地。今天讲三件事：呼吸问题和早产儿；新生儿保暖和低血糖处理；以及抽搐、危险的呕吐、产伤和转运。

slides.title: Meconium in the fluid
slides.body:
• Green-black fluid: the baby passed stool before birth, often from stress
  • In 10–15% of births; more if post-term or small
  • Risk: blocked airways, lung inflammation, pneumothorax
  • Vigorous (crying, good tone): routine care
  • Not vigorous (limp, HR < 100, poor breathing): usual steps, BVM
  • Routine tracheal suctioning: no longer recommended
slides.say: Meconium is the baby's first stool. A baby stressed before or during birth may pass it into the amniotic fluid, which then looks green or black. This happens in ten to fifteen percent of births, more often in post-term or small babies. Breathed in, it can block the airways, inflame the lungs and cause a pneumothorax. So look at the baby. Vigorous, crying with good tone? Routine care. Not vigorous, limp, with a heart rate under one hundred or poor breathing? Follow the usual resuscitation steps, including bag-valve-mask ventilation. Routine suctioning through a tracheal tube is no longer recommended.
slides.sayZh: 胎粪是孩子的第一次大便。孩子在出生前或出生时受到应激，可能把它排进羊水，羊水就变成绿色或黑色。约百分之十到十五的分娩会出现，过期产或偏小的孩子更常见。吸进去的话，可能堵塞气道、引起肺部炎症，甚至气胸。所以要看孩子本身。有活力，哭声好、肌张力好？按常规处理。没有活力，松软、心率低于一百或呼吸差？按常规复苏步骤，包括球囊面罩通气。现在已经不再推荐常规经气管导管吸引。

slides.title: Breathing trouble: clues to the cause
slides.body:
• Most common single cause: prematurity
  • Distress: retractions, nasal flaring, grunting, pauses
  • Blue and working hard: lungs, sepsis, severe acidosis
  • Blue but breathing easily: think a heart defect
  • Apnea = pause of 20 s or more
  • Primary apnea: stimulation works. Secondary: needs BVM
slides.say: When a newborn is breathing but struggling, look for retractions, nasal flaring, grunting and pauses. Prematurity is the most common single cause. The work of breathing is a clue: a baby who is blue and working hard usually has a lung problem, sepsis or severe acidosis, while a baby who is blue but breathing easily points to a heart defect. Apnea means a pause of twenty seconds or more. After a short period of hypoxia, the baby is in primary apnea, and drying and stimulation can restart breathing. If hypoxia continues, the baby gasps and enters secondary apnea; stimulation won't work any more, and it needs bag-valve-mask ventilation.
slides.sayZh: 新生儿有呼吸但很吃力时，要看有没有三凹征、鼻翼扇动、呼气呻吟和呼吸停顿。早产是最常见的单一原因。呼吸费不费力是条线索：发绀又费力，通常是肺部问题、败血症或严重酸中毒；发绀但呼吸轻松，要想到心脏畸形。呼吸暂停是指停顿二十秒或更长。短时间缺氧后，孩子处于原发性呼吸暂停，擦干和刺激可以让呼吸恢复。如果缺氧持续，孩子会喘息，然后进入继发性呼吸暂停，这时刺激已经没用，必须用球囊面罩通气。

slides.title: Air or bowel where lungs should be
slides.body:
PneumothoraxDiaphragmatic hernia
Cluesudden worsening, often during PPVsunken belly; bowel sounds in the chest
Chestone side quiet; heart sounds shiftusually left quiet; heart sounds shift right
Firstrecheck your ventilationbook: tube + gastric tube, not mask breaths

The book's needle decompression is not on the BC licensing exam.
slides.say: Two problems put air or bowel where the lungs should be. A pneumothorax is air leaking around a lung: the baby suddenly worsens, often during ventilation, with one side quiet. First, recheck your own ventilation. A diaphragmatic hernia is a hole in the diaphragm, usually on the left, that lets bowel into the chest. Look for a sunken belly, quiet breath sounds on the left, and heart sounds pushed right. Mask breaths blow air into that bowel; the book's answer is a tracheal tube, a gastric tube, and a centre with neonatal intensive care and surgery. Needle decompression isn't on the BC licensing exam; in BCEHS it's an ACP skill.
slides.sayZh: 有两种问题会让空气或肠子占据肺的位置。气胸是空气漏到肺的周围：孩子突然变差，常在通气过程中，一侧呼吸音减弱。先复查你自己的通气。膈疝是膈肌上有个洞，通常在左侧，让肠子进入胸腔。要看腹部凹陷、左侧呼吸音减弱、心音被推向右边。面罩通气会把气吹进这些肠子；原书的做法是气管插管、胃管，并送往有新生儿重症监护和外科的中心。针刺减压不在 BC 执照考试范围内；在 BCEHS，它属于 ACP 技能。

slides.q: Minutes after birth, a term baby is in worsening distress. The belly looks sunken, breath sounds are quiet on the left, and heart sounds are loudest on the right. What should you suspect?
slides.say: Quick question. Minutes after birth, a term baby is in worsening distress. The belly looks sunken, breath sounds are quiet on the left, and the heart sounds are loudest on the right. What should you suspect? A, a pneumothorax on the right. B, a diaphragmatic hernia. C, meconium aspiration. D, a heart defect alone. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来道快问快答。出生几分钟后，一个足月儿呼吸窘迫越来越重：腹部凹陷，左侧呼吸音减弱，心音在右侧最响。你应该怀疑什么？A 右侧气胸；B 膈疝；C 胎粪吸入；D 单纯心脏畸形。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, a diaphragmatic hernia. The sunken belly is the key clue: the bowel has moved up into the chest, usually on the left, pushing the heart to the right. A is wrong because a right-sided pneumothorax would quiet the right side. C doesn't empty the belly. D is wrong because a heart defect alone causes cyanosis without much work of breathing, and it doesn't quiet one side of the chest.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，膈疝。腹部凹陷是关键线索：肠子跑进了胸腔，通常在左侧，把心脏推向右边。A 错，右侧气胸应该是右侧呼吸音减弱。C 不会让腹部变空。D 错，单纯心脏畸形引起的是发绀而呼吸不太费力，也不会让一侧胸部呼吸音减弱。

slides.title: Preterm babies
slides.body:
• Preterm: before 37 weeks; low birth weight: under 2,500 g
  • Very preterm: into a plastic bag undried; dry the head, add a hat
  • Lungs lack surfactant: use the lowest pressure that works
  • Too much O₂ harms eyes and lungs; book target SpO₂ 90–95%
  • But never withhold O₂ from a blue baby
  • Any signs of life: resuscitate and keep warm
slides.say: Preterm means born before thirty-seven weeks; low birth weight means under two thousand five hundred grams, usually from prematurity. These babies lose heat very fast, so a very preterm baby goes straight into a plastic bag up to the neck, without drying the body; dry the head and add a hat. Their lungs lack surfactant, which keeps the air sacs open, so use the lowest pressure that moves the chest. Too much oxygen harms the eyes and lungs, so the book aims for a saturation of ninety to ninety-five percent. But never withhold oxygen from a blue baby. If there are signs of life, resuscitate.
slides.sayZh: 早产是不足三十七周出生；低出生体重是不到两千五百克，通常由早产引起。这些孩子散热非常快，所以很早的早产儿出生后直接装进塑料袋，套到脖子，身体不擦干；擦干头部并戴帽子。他们的肺缺乏表面活性物质，也就是让肺泡保持张开的物质，所以只用能让胸廓起伏的最低压力。氧气太多会伤害眼睛和肺，所以原书把血氧目标定在百分之九十到九十五。但绝不能对发绀的孩子停氧。只要有生命迹象，就要复苏。

slides.title: Keeping newborns warm
slides.body:
Heat lossExamplePrevent it
Evaporationwet skindry fast, remove wet towels
Convectiondraftsclose doors, warm the ambulance
Conductioncold surfacesskin-to-skin, warm blankets
Radiationcold objects nearbywarm room, about 23–26°C

Hypothermia: below 36°C. Newborns can't shiver. No hot water bottles.
slides.say: Newborns can't shiver. They make heat by burning brown fat, which uses oxygen and glucose, and their large skin surface makes them cool fast. Heat leaves by evaporation from wet skin, convection to moving air, conduction to cold surfaces, and radiation to cold objects nearby. So dry the baby, remove wet towels, close doors, warm the ambulance and go skin-to-skin; the book suggests a room of about twenty-three to twenty-six degrees. Hypothermia, below thirty-six degrees, causes apnea, a slow heart rate, low sugar and acidosis, and a cold baby may be septic. Never use hot water bottles; they burn.
slides.sayZh: 新生儿不会寒战。他们靠燃烧棕色脂肪产热，这会消耗氧气和葡萄糖；皮肤面积相对大，所以降温很快。热量通过湿皮肤蒸发、流动空气对流、接触冷表面传导，以及向附近冷物体辐射而散失。所以要擦干孩子、拿走湿毛巾、关门、给救护车加温、皮肤贴皮肤；原书建议室温约二十三到二十六度。低于三十六度就是低体温，会引起呼吸暂停、心率慢、低血糖和酸中毒，而且体温低的孩子可能有败血症。绝不要用热水袋，会烫伤。

slides.title: Low blood sugar in newborns
slides.body:
• At risk: small or large for dates, preterm, diabetic mother
  • Also: cold, sepsis, hypoxia, a difficult birth
  • Signs: jittery, floppy, poor feeding, apnea, low temp, seizures
  • Check BGL in every sick newborn (heel stick)
  • BC: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L at every age; no newborn number
  • Book: 2.6 mmol/L threshold; BC IV dextrose is D10W only
slides.say: A newborn's sugar can drop fast. A term baby's glycogen stores last only about eight to twelve hours, and some babies run low sooner: those small or large for their age, preterm babies, babies of diabetic mothers, and babies stressed by cold, sepsis or hypoxia. The signs are vague: jittery, floppy, feeding poorly, apnea, a low temperature, or seizures. So check the glucose in every sick newborn with a heel stick. Here's the BC point. The book uses a newborn threshold of two point six. BC uses one threshold for all ages, a glucose below four point zero, with no separate newborn number, and the only IV dextrose is D10W.
slides.sayZh: 新生儿的血糖可能掉得很快。足月儿的糖原储备只够大约八到十二小时，有些孩子更早耗尽：小于或大于胎龄儿、早产儿、糖尿病母亲的孩子，以及受到寒冷、败血症或缺氧应激的孩子。症状很模糊：颤抖、松软、吃奶差、呼吸暂停、体温低或抽搐。所以每个生病的新生儿都要扎足跟测血糖。BC 的要点是：原书用的新生儿阈值是二点六；BC 各年龄统一一个阈值，血糖低于四点零，没有单独的新生儿数值，而且静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。

slides.q: A jittery 2-day-old is feeding poorly. BGL is 3.2 mmol/L. Using the BC rules, how should you treat this reading?
options: As normal, because the newborn threshold is 2.6
As hypoglycemia, because BC treats BGL below 4.0 at every age
Recheck in an hour before acting
Give D50W, the standard IV dextrose
slides.say: Now a BC question. A jittery two-day-old is feeding poorly. The blood glucose is three point two. Using the BC rules, how should you treat this reading? A, as normal, because the newborn threshold is two point six. B, as hypoglycemia, because BC treats a glucose below four point zero at every age. C, recheck in an hour before acting. D, give D50W, the standard IV dextrose. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 BC 题。一个两天大的孩子在颤抖、吃奶差，血糖三点二。按 BC 规则，这个读数该怎么处理？A 当作正常，因为新生儿阈值是二点六；B 当作低血糖，因为 BC 各年龄都把低于四点零当作低血糖；C 一小时后复测再说；D 给 D50W，标准的静脉葡萄糖。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. BC uses one hypoglycemia threshold for all ages, a glucose below four point zero, with no separate newborn number, so three point two is low, and this baby has symptoms. A uses the book's number, not BC's. C wastes time in a baby who already has symptoms. D is wrong because BC has no D50W; the only IV dextrose is D10W.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 各年龄只有一个低血糖阈值，低于四点零，没有单独的新生儿数值，所以三点二就是低，而且这个孩子已经有症状。A 用的是原书的数字，不是 BC 的。C 对已有症状的孩子是在浪费时间。D 错，BC 没有 D50W，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。

slides.title: Seizure or jitteriness?
slides.body:
JitterinessSeizure
Eyesnormaldeviation or staring
Set off by touchyesno
Movementtremorjerking
Gently hold the limbit stopsit doesn't stop

Seizures are often subtle: blinking, sucking, pedalling, apnea. Check BGL first.
slides.say: Newborn seizures rarely look like adult seizures. They're often subtle: eye deviation, blinking, sucking, pedalling movements of the legs, or apnea. Jitteriness can look similar, so here's a simple test: gently hold the moving limb. Jitteriness stops; a seizure doesn't. Jitteriness is also set off by touch and has no eye signs. Common causes include low oxygen around birth, low sugar, low calcium and drug withdrawal. Your first move is the blood glucose, then oxygen and ventilation as needed. The book's seizure drugs, lorazepam, phenobarbital and phenytoin, aren't on the BC licensing exam, and neither are any benzodiazepines.
slides.sayZh: 新生儿抽搐很少像成人抽搐。它常常很隐蔽：眼球偏斜、眨眼、吸吮动作、双腿蹬踏，或呼吸暂停。颤抖看起来可能很像，所以有个简单的测试：轻轻握住正在动的肢体。颤抖会停，抽搐不会停。颤抖还会因触碰而诱发，而且没有眼部表现。常见原因包括出生前后缺氧、低血糖、低血钙和药物戒断。你的第一步是测血糖，然后按需给氧和通气。原书的抗惊厥药劳拉西泮、苯巴比妥和苯妥英，都不在 BC 执照考试范围内，苯二氮卓类也都不考。

slides.title: Red flags: vomiting and birth injuries
slides.body:
• Green vomit = twisted bowel until proven otherwise
  • Forceful, non-green vomiting at about 3 weeks: pyloric stenosis
  • Dehydration: dry mouth, HR > 160, sunken fontanelle
  • Caput: soft scalp swelling, gone in 1–2 days
  • Spreading scalp swelling: subgaleal bleed, can cause shock
  • Won't move one arm: clavicle fracture or brachial plexus injury
slides.say: Two groups of red flags. Most newborns spit up, but green, or bilious, vomit means a twisted bowel until proven otherwise; it cuts off the gut's blood supply, so it's a surgical emergency. Forceful, non-green vomiting at around three weeks suggests pyloric stenosis. Watch for dehydration: a dry mouth, a heart rate over one hundred sixty, a sunken fontanelle. Now birth injuries. Soft scalp swelling, called caput, fades in a day or two. But a spreading swelling under the scalp, especially after a vacuum delivery, may be a subgaleal bleed that can cause shock; never drain it. A baby who won't move one arm may have a broken clavicle or a brachial plexus injury.
slides.sayZh: 两组危险信号。大多数新生儿都会吐奶，但绿色的、也就是含胆汁的呕吐，在排除之前都按肠扭转处理；它会切断肠道血供，属于外科急症。三周左右喷射性、不带绿色的呕吐，要想到幽门狭窄。注意脱水：口干、心率超过一百六十、囟门凹陷。再看产伤。头皮软软的肿胀叫产瘤，一两天就消。但头皮下越来越大的肿胀，尤其在胎吸助产后，可能是帽状腱膜下出血，可引起休克，绝不要去抽。孩子一只胳膊不动，可能是锁骨骨折或臂丛神经损伤。

slides.title: Transport and the family
slides.body:
• Nearest facility with the right level of care
  • May be a closer community hospital, not the biggest centre
  • Call ahead; special care needed? Agree the destination
  • En route: temperature, effort, airway, colour, HR, SpO₂, BGL
  • Tell the family what you're doing; don't quote survival odds
slides.say: Where do you go? The book says the nearest facility that can give the right level of care, which isn't always the biggest centre; a closer community hospital may stabilize a very sick baby first. Call ahead, and when the baby needs special care, like extreme prematurity or surgery, agree on the destination with medical direction. En route, keep watching temperature, breathing effort, airway, colour and heart rate, and check the saturation and glucose. Tell the family what you're doing and what comes next, but don't quote survival odds. If you don't know an answer, say so, and tell them who will know.
slides.sayZh: 去哪里？原书说：去能提供合适级别照护的最近机构，不一定是最大的中心；更近的社区医院也许能先稳定病情很重的孩子。要提前联系；孩子需要特殊照护，比如极早产或手术时，要和医疗指导商定目的地。途中持续观察体温、呼吸用力、气道、肤色和心率，并测血氧和血糖。告诉家属你在做什么、下一步是什么，但不要报存活率。答不上来就如实说，并告诉他们谁能回答。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: low sugar in a newborn
slides.body:
BC Diabetic Emergencies: decreased LOC; treat BGL < 4.0 mmol/L

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Airway, O₂, BGL with the baseline vitals
  • BGL < 4.0, airway protected: oral glucose
  • EMR: airway not protected → glucagon

PCP adds

  • Vascular access (IV)
  • Confirmed low → D10W; BC gives no newborn dose
  • Book: D10W 2 mL/kg, ordered by medical direction
  • Glucagon only if no IV
slides.say: For low sugar, the BC Diabetic Emergencies protocol covers a patient with a decreased level of consciousness, and its threshold, below four point zero, applies at every age. Every licence level manages the airway, gives oxygen and checks the glucose. If the airway is protected, oral glucose; for an EMR, if it isn't, glucagon. The PCP adds IV access, D10W for confirmed hypoglycemia, and glucagon only when there's no IV. Be careful with doses: the BC D10W dose of ten to twenty-five grams isn't weight-based, and the BC sources give no newborn dose. The book's newborn dose is two millilitres per kilogram, ordered by medical direction.
slides.sayZh: 低血糖方面，BC 的糖尿病急症流程适用于意识水平下降的病人，阈值低于四点零，各年龄通用。所有执照级别都要管理气道、给氧、测血糖。气道能自我保护就给口服葡萄糖；对 EMR 来说，气道不能保护就给胰高血糖素。PCP 多了静脉通路、确认低血糖后给 D10W，没有静脉通路时才用胰高血糖素。剂量要小心：BC 的 D10W 剂量十到二十五克不是按体重算的，BC 资料没有给新生儿剂量。原书的新生儿剂量是每公斤两毫升，由医疗指导下达。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Diphenhydramine: contraindicated in neonates (BC)
  • Ondansetron: BC child dose starts at 6 months
  • Ipratropium: not for neonates under 30 days (BC)
  • Opioids in mom: ventilate first; book warns of naloxone seizures
  • Newborn fever or low temperature: think serious infection
  • Bilious vomit or a spreading scalp swelling: go now
slides.say: Your bigger drug box brings new newborn traps. In the BC monographs, diphenhydramine is contraindicated in neonates, ondansetron's paediatric dose starts at six months, and ipratropium is not for neonates under thirty days. For a newborn depressed by opioids, ventilate first. The book warns that if the mother has used opioids long-term, naloxone can trigger dangerous seizures in the baby. Fever in a newborn is serious: about thirteen percent of babies under twenty-eight days with a temperature over thirty-eight point one have a serious bacterial infection, and an infected newborn may be cold instead of hot. And green vomit or a spreading scalp swelling means move now.
slides.sayZh: 药箱变大了，新生儿的新陷阱也来了。按 BC 药物专论：苯海拉明新生儿禁用；昂丹司琼的儿童剂量从六个月起；异丙托溴铵不用于三十天以内的新生儿。被阿片类抑制的新生儿，先通气。原书警告：如果母亲长期使用阿片类，给纳洛酮可能让孩子出现危险的抽搐。新生儿发热很严重：二十八天以内、体温超过三十八点一度的孩子，约百分之十三有严重细菌感染；而且感染的新生儿可能不是发热，而是体温低。还有，绿色呕吐或头皮肿胀不断扩大，要立刻出发。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Hypoglycemia: BGL < 4.0 mmol/L at every age; not the book's 2.6
  • IV dextrose: D10W only, no D50W
  • Lorazepam, phenobarbital, phenytoin, bicarbonate: not on the exam
  • No benzodiazepines or tracheal drugs on the exam
  • Needle decompression: not on the exam; an ACP skill in BCEHS
  • Naloxone: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV, or 4 mg IN
slides.say: Now the book versus BC. The book's newborn hypoglycemia threshold is two point six; BC uses below four point zero at every age, and the only IV dextrose is D10W. The book's lorazepam, phenobarbital, phenytoin and sodium bicarbonate aren't on the BC licensing exam, and neither are benzodiazepines, tracheal drugs or needle decompression, which is an ACP skill in BCEHS. The book gives newborn naloxone by weight, zero point one milligrams per kilogram. BC naloxone doses are fixed, point four, point four, point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, or four milligrams intranasal, with no separate newborn dose. Either way, ventilation comes first.
slides.sayZh: 现在对比原书和 BC。原书的新生儿低血糖阈值是二点六；BC 各年龄都用低于四点零，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。原书的劳拉西泮、苯巴比妥、苯妥英和碳酸氢钠都不在 BC 执照考试范围内，苯二氮卓类、经气管给药和针刺减压也都不考；针刺减压在 BCEHS 属于 ACP 技能。原书的新生儿纳洛酮按体重给，每公斤零点一毫克；BC 的纳洛酮是固定剂量：零点四、零点四、零点八、再两毫克，肌注或静注，或鼻内四毫克，没有单独的新生儿剂量。不管哪种，通气都放在第一位。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Breathing: blue + hard work = lungs; blue + easy = heart; sunken belly = hernia
  2. Warmth and sugar: dry, hat, skin-to-skin; BC BGL < 4.0, D10W only
  3. Red flags: green vomit, spreading scalp swelling, subtle seizures

Next: Chapter 44, Pediatrics
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: breathing clues. Blue and working hard points to the lungs; blue but breathing easily points to the heart; a sunken belly with a quiet left chest points to a diaphragmatic hernia. Two: warmth and sugar. Dry, hat, skin-to-skin, and check the glucose in every sick newborn; in BC, below four point zero is low at every age, and the only IV dextrose is D10W. Three: red flags. Green vomit, a spreading scalp swelling and subtle seizures need fast action, and check every drug's newborn limits. Next, Chapter 44: pediatrics. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，呼吸线索：发绀又费力，指向肺；发绀但呼吸轻松，指向心脏；腹部凹陷加左胸呼吸音弱，指向膈疝。二，保暖和血糖：擦干、戴帽、皮肤贴皮肤，每个生病的新生儿都测血糖；在 BC，各年龄低于四点零都算低，静脉葡萄糖只有 D10W。三，危险信号：绿色呕吐、不断扩大的头皮肿胀和隐蔽的抽搐都要快速处理，并核对每种药的新生儿限制。下一章，第四十四章：儿科。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
